Now, what does the float switch do? For a low-level cutoff, you want to detect when water is low. Typically, a float switch for low level is mounted so that when water drops below a certain point, the float drops and the switch changes state. There are two types: normally open (NO) or normally closed (NC). If the switch is NO, it closes when water is low. If NC, it opens when water is low. The design uses a pull-up, so the default (switch open) is high. If the switch is NO (closes when water low), then water low -> switch closed -> NET0021 low. Then T5 base low -> T5 off -> main pump gate pulled up by R1 -> pump ON. That would mean water low turns pump ON. That's wrong. If the switch is NC (opens when water low), then water low -> switch open -> NET0021 high. Then T5 base high -> T5 on -> gate low -> pump OFF. That would mean water low turns pump OFF.
